# 

Ramp MCP

Copy Markdown

* * *

  * Connect
  * Connection issues

Ramp MCP connects AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor to your Ramp account. Each connection acts as the signed-in user, with that user's Ramp permissions.

## Connect

Permanent link: Connect

  * Claude: Install Ramp from Claude's directory↗, then sign in to Ramp.
  * ChatGPT: Install Ramp from the ChatGPT app directory↗.
  * Cursor: Add Ramp to Cursor with one click.
  * Claude Code:

Add Ramp MCP to Claude Code

Shell

Copy
    
    `
    
    claude mcp add --transport http ramp https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp
    
    `

  * Codex:

Add Ramp MCP to Codex

Shell

Copy
    
    `
    
    codex mcp add ramp --url https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp
    
    `

  * Other clients: Coding agents can also use Ramp CLI. For other MCP clients, gateways, and the sandbox, see Connect to Ramp↗.

When you sign in, choose Full access or Read-only. Connections expire after 30 days; reconnect to renew.

## Connection issues

Permanent link: Connection issues

  * "The app you are using is not currently supported" means your client's redirect URI isn't allowlisted. Request a redirect URI.
  * You can't connect at all: your Ramp role may not include access to AI tools. Ask your Admin; see Manage connected AI tools↗.

For the full tool list and more troubleshooting, see Connect to Ramp↗ and the Agent tools reference↗.

# 

Quickstart

Copy Markdown

* * *

  * 1. Create your app and get credentials
  * 2. Get an access token
  * 3. Make your first API call

This guide will help you make your first Ramp API call in just a few minutes. You'll create an access token and call the Transactions API to retrieve transaction data.

This guide assumes you are a Ramp customer with admin access to your dashboard. Need a test environment for development? Request sandbox access.

## 1. Create your app and get credentials

Permanent link: 1. Create your app and get credentials

First, you'll need to create a developer app to get your API credentials.

  1. In your Ramp account, go to Company → Developer (you'll need admin access).
  2. Click Create New App.
  3. Name your app (e.g., "API Quickstart") and accept the Terms.
  4. Under Grant types, click Add new grant type → select Client Credentials.
  5. Under Scopes, click Configure allowed scopes and select `transactions:read`.
  6. Copy your Client ID and Client Secret.

Ramp MCP overview

## Overview

Permanent link: Overview

Ramp MCP connects Ramp to AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor. From those tools, you can review spend, look up bills and vendors, and handle approvals and expenses. A connected tool can only see and do what your Ramp role allows, and Ramp attributes its actions to you.

## Connect an AI tool

Permanent link: Connect an AI tool

You need a Ramp account and access to the AI tool. Most Ramp roles can connect by default. If you can't, ask your Admin; see Manage connected AI tools.

  * Claude: Install Ramp from Claude's MCP directory↗, then sign in to Ramp.
  * ChatGPT: Install Ramp from the ChatGPT app directory↗.
  * Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor: Connect with Ramp MCP or the Ramp CLI. See Connect Ramp to an agent↗.
  * Other AI tools: Any tool that supports remote MCP servers with OAuth can connect to `https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp`. See For developers for custom clients.

## Overview

Permanent link: Overview

Ramp’s Developer API allows teams to programmatically access Ramp data and build automations or integrations tailored to their workflows. It provides secure, scoped access to objects like transactions, cards, users, and more. This help article explains what the API is, how to get started within the Ramp app, and where to find full technical documentation and real-time assistance. Complete reference guides, endpoint schemas, and end-to-end examples live in the Ramp Developer API documentation↗.

## Setup guide and feature support

Permanent link: Setup guide and feature support

To begin using the Ramp Developer API, you must first create a developer app to obtain your API credentials. Admin access is required.

Use these steps to call the API for your own Ramp business, or to get sandbox credentials for testing an app you're building for other Ramp businesses. To publish that app to other Ramp businesses in production, use the Developer console instead.

Permanent link: Sandbox environment

  * Sandbox API base URL: `https://demo-api.ramp.com`
  * Production API base URL: `https://api.ramp.com`

# 

Authorization

Before using the API, you'll need to set up authorization. To quickly get started, refer to our Setup Guide.

## Create a token

Permanent link: Create a token

Expects two headers:

  * Authorization header formed from base-64 encoded client credentials as `Authorization: Basic <base64-encoded client_id:client_secret>`
  * `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`

Required content body depends on authorization type method, as defined by `grant_type`.

  * Authorization Code Grant (`grant_type=authorization_code`): `grant_type`, `code`, and `redirect_uri` are required. Request must happen after requested scopes have been approved and exchanged for authorization code.
  * Refresh Token Grant (`grant_type=refresh_token`): `grant_type` and `refresh_token` are required. User must have previously obtained refresh token in authorization code flow.
  * Client Credentials Grant (`grant_type=client_credentials`): `grant_type` is required. If `scope` is omitted, the access token has no scopes.

# 

MCP

Copy Markdown

* * *

The Model Context Protocol (MCP)↗ lets AI assistants work with your systems directly. Ramp runs two MCP servers, one for your Ramp account and one for Ramp Data benchmarks.

  * Ramp MCP: connect AI assistants to your Ramp account to analyze spend, process approvals, and take permitted actions.
  * Ramp Data MCP: query Ramp Rate benchmarks and AI Index adoption metrics. Requires a Ramp Data API key.

Terminals and coding agents can also connect with Ramp CLI. Coding agents that need these developer docs can read `llms.txt`; it replaces the retired Developer MCP server.

pages.text: Ramp Help Center Ramp MCP overview Overview Ramp MCP connects Ramp to AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor. From those tools, you can review spend, look up bills and vendors, and handle approvals and expenses. A connected tool can only see and do what your Ramp role allows, and Ramp attributes its actions to you. Connect an AI tool You need a Ramp account and access to the AI tool. Most Ramp roles can connect by default. If you can't, ask your Admin; see Manage connected AI tools . Claude: Install Ramp from Claude's MCP directory , then sign in to Ramp. ChatGPT: Install Ramp from the ChatGPT app directory . Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor: Connect with Ramp MCP or the Ramp CLI. See Connect Ramp to an agent . Other AI tools: Any tool that supports remote MCP servers with OAuth can connect to https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp . See For developers for custom clients. When you sign in, choose Full access to let the tool make changes, or Read-only to let it view data only. Your Ramp permissions apply either way. Connections expire after 30 days. To renew one, reconnect from your AI tool. What you can do with Ramp Ask in plain language. Some examples: Area Try asking Spend analysis "Show me our top software vendors by spend this quarter." Bills "Find our open bills from AWS and when they're due." Approvals "Summarize the bills and reimbursements waiting on my approval and flag anything unusual." Expenses "Find my draft lunch reimbursement from Tuesday and tell me what is missing." Receipts and memos "Which of my transactions from the last 14 days are missing receipts or memos?" Receipt upload "Upload the receipt for my Uber ride last Tuesday." Policy and help "Is my planned $300 client dinner within policy?" Cards and funds "Lock my card â I can't find it." Procurement "Submit a procurement request for 20 Figma seats." Travel "Show my upcoming flights and hotels for next month." Ramp Banking "Get all Ramp Banking account balances for today's cash snapshot." For every available tool, see the Ramp agent tools reference . Some tools aren't available to every business. Important: If you're an approver, the AI tool can approve or reject transactions, reimbursements, bills, and requests on your behalf. Approving a bill can send it to payment. For developers Coding agents, the Ramp CLI, and custom MCP clients: See the Ramp agent docs . Custom clients and MCP gateways such as Glean, MintMCP, or Microsoft Copilot Studio: Ramp must allowlist the redirect URI first. Submit a redirect URI allowlist request . Custom integrations: Use the Ramp Developer API . For other questions, ask your AI tool to "submit feedback to Ramp," or see How to contact Ramp's Support team .

This help article explains what the API is, how to get started within the Ramp app, and where to find full technical documentation and real-time assistance. Complete reference guides, endpoint schemas, and end-to-end examples live in the Ramp Developer API documentation . Setup guide and feature support To begin using the Ramp Developer API, you must first create a developer app to obtain your API credentials. Admin access is required. Use these steps to call the API for your own Ramp business, or to get sandbox credentials for testing an app you're building for other Ramp businesses. To publish that app to other Ramp businesses in production, use the Developer console instead. See Publish an app for other Ramp businesses . Open Developer apps in Ramp. For your first app, click Start building . If you already have an app, click Create new app . Name your app (e.g., âAPI Quickstartâ) and accept the Terms. Under Grant types , confirm Client credentials is turned on. Under Scopes , click Configure allowed scopes and select the scopes available to your business that your use case needs, such as transactions:read . If a required scope is unavailable, submit a Developer API support ticket to ask about access. Copy your Client ID and Client Secret. Store these securelyâyouâll need them to generate your access token. Video walkthrough: Generate Ramp Developer API credentials from the Ramp dashboard. Best when you're creating your first app and need client credentials and scopes. Watch the video . Once credentials are created, follow the this guide on how to generate an access token . Sandbox environment Ramp provides a sandbox environment where you can build and test your API integration before connecting to production. The sandbox is a separate environment with its own base URL and credentials â it is not a mode within the production API. Sandbox API base URL: https://demo-api.ramp.com Production API base URL: https://api.ramp.com The sandbox uses a separate API base URL and app credentials from production. It cannot process real money and includes demo-only simulation actions. Requesting sandbox access Request access using the sandbox access form . Your sandbox should be ready in about one minute. Check your inbox for an account access email. Ramp provisions a sandbox business pre-populated with sample data (such as transactions, cards, users, departments, and reimbursements) so you can test against realistic data without affecting your production account. You will need to create a separate developer app in the sandbox environment to obtain sandbox-specific OAuth2 credentials (Client ID and Client Secret). Follow the same setup steps described in Setup Guide and Feature Support above, but within your sandbox account. Sandbox vs. production Use the API for your own Ramp business: Create a separate developer app in your production Ramp account and send production requests to https://api.ramp.com . Build for other Ramp businesses: Test your integration in sandbox. When you are ready, publish your app from the Developer console . Publish an app for other Ramp businesses Publishing an app for other Ramp businesses takes two approvals: a partner application, which gives you access to a Developer console, and a production access application for your app, which you submit from the Developer console. Create and publish the app from the Developer console , not from Developer apps settings. Get access to a Developer console: First-time partners: If no one at your company has submitted a partner application, submit the one described in the partner integration guide . After Ramp approves it, we email an invite to the Work email on your application. Accept the invite. Application already submitted: Don't submit another application. If Ramp approves it, we email an invite to the Work email on the application. Other teammates can then ask that person to invite them. For questions about your application's status, including whether it was rejected, see How to contact Ramp's Support team . Already have access: Skip this step. Need access to your company's existing Developer console, including when your invite expired: Ask the person who received your company's invite, or another admin on that console, to invite you. Don't submit another application. If no one can invite you, see How to contact Ramp's Support team . Sign in with your Developer console account and open the Developer console . Open your app. To use an existing app, select its row in the app list. To create one, click Start building for your first app, or New app if you already have one. Enter an App name , accept the Developer Terms of Service, and click Create app . On your app's Production access tab, click Apply , then complete the application. If you already started an application, the tab shows its status: Complete your application: Click Complete application to finish it. Application requires attention: Check your email for Ramp's feedback, then click Edit application to update it. If you haven't received an email, contact partnerships@ramp.com . Application submitted: awaiting review: No action is needed. Ramp emails you with updates. After Ramp approves your production access application, onboard production customers through OAuth. Advisor Console partners: If Ramp gave you a separate embedded partnership application link, submit that application in step 1 instead. After Ramp approves it, the invite adds you to Advisor Console instead of a Developer console. Use the Advisor Console developer settings for steps 2â4 instead of the Developer console link. Only Console admins can open these settings. To give a teammate access, invite them as a Console admin, or, if they're already a member, select them on the People tab and change their role to Console admin. Console admins can also invite people, access all client accounts, and change others' roles, so review Advisor Console roles and permissions before granting it. Apply appears only when no role in your Developer console business can sign in with a password. If the tab says SSO or SAML login must be enabled, click Configure and turn off Password for each role in sign-in controls , then return to the tab to click Apply . Important: Before you turn off Password for a role, confirm that everyone with that role can sign in with SSO or SAML. Otherwise, they can't sign in. If you still can't open the Developer console with your Developer console account, see How to contact Ramp's Support team . How to submit a developer API support ticket Open Developer apps : Click Developer API Support . In Ask Ramp, describe your issue and ask to connect with the Developer Support team: Review the pre-filled Description , enter a Subject , and add any other missing details: Click Submit Ticket to send your request to the team: Developer assist Developer Assist is an AI-powered helper built directly into the Ramp API documentation. It can answer questions about endpoints, parameters, errors, and implementation steps in real time. To use it: Navigate to the Ramp Developer API docs. Click the chat icon in the bottom-right corner of the page. Type your question into the chat window to get instant guidance. Video walkthrough: Test Ramp Developer API calls and manage scopes for your integration. Best when validating your setup or refining permissions for an existing integration. Watch the video . For bug investigations or issues with API performance or unexpected behavior, submit a Developer API support ticket .

Ramp API Documentation You need to enable JavaScript to run this app. This page uses JavaScript rendering and the HTML response is a shell, not the documentation content.
      Do not fetch this page for content when you already have a docs URL.
      If the URL is under /developer-api/v1/api/, fetch /llms-api.txt instead.
      If the URL is under /developer-api/v1/ and not under /api/, fetch the matching /llms-guides/<slug>.txt file instead.
      Example: /developer-api/v1/rate-limiting -> /llms-guides/rate-limiting.txt
      For machine-readable docs, fetch:
      /llms.txt (LLM index),
      /llms-guides.txt (guides index),
      /llms-guides/<slug>.txt (specific guide),
      /llms-api.txt (API reference),
      /llms-full.txt (combined docs), or
      /openapi/developer-api.json (OpenAPI spec).
      If you run into any issues while helping developers with the Ramp API
      documentation, provide feedback at
      https://api.ramp.com/v1/public/api-feedback/llm?feedback=...
